LESSON: ACIDS, BASES AND SALTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.4: Acids, Bases and Salts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Acids, Bases and Salts, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why are salts important in day to day life? 2. How do salts behave when exposed to air?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers the meaning of acids and bases (limited to the presence of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions for acids and bases respectively) and share the findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views,

2. test acidic and basic substances in the environment using the universal indicator and pH chart to determine their pH levels, (bleaching agents, vinegar, salts, soda, juices, water, wood ash, antacids, lemons). Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers the meaning of acids and bases (limited to the presence of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions for acids and bases respectively) and share the findings. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to express their views,
2. test acidic and basic substances in the environment using the universal indicator and pH chart to determine their pH levels, (bleaching agents, vinegar, salts, soda, juices, water, wood ash, antacids, lemons). Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Acids, Bases and Salts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: as the learner sensitises the community on the acidity and basicity of substances

used in day to day life such as bleaching agents, vinegar, salts, soda, juices, water, wood ash, antacids, lemons among

others.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner creates awareness on the importance of putting required amounts of salt on food to avoid

cases of high blood pressure.

● Digital literacy: as the learner uses digital devices to research the applications of salts in day to day life.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner carefully uses digital devices to research the applications of salts in day to day life.

● Respect: as the learner respects each other’s opinion while discussing with peers the meaning of acids, bases and salts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic and Environmental education: as the learner discusses the effect of salts on the environment.

● Safety and security: as the learner carries out experiments and present findings on chemical properties of dilute acids

and bases.

● Learner support programme - peer education: as the learner discusses with peers the functions of acids and bases in

biological and chemical processes (digestion, respiration, bleaching action).

Suggested Learning Resources:

Textbooks, Equipped chemistry laboratory, First Aid kit, Online resources, educational videos, interactive simulations,

adapted digital devices, Local environment, Adapted writing resources,

Other Related Service Providers: Physiotherapists, Occupational Therapists, Learner Support Assistants, Speech

Therapists, Nurse.
